title: Tight Complexity of Linearization-Based LowMC Key Recovery
summary: Existing analysis gives only an upper bound for extended linearization-based LowMC key recovery; a simple, tight expected-time formula accounting for the equation–variable tradeoff remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine a simple, tight formula for the expected time required by linearization-based full-key recovery against LowMC from $N$ compact differential trails when the attack is extended backward by more than $b+r_3$ rounds under the condition $b\le r_1+r_2$. The formula must capture the tradeoff that extending the attack can reveal more linear equations but requires additional variables to linearize inactive S-boxes: each inactive S-box introduces three extra variables, whereas each active S-box yields only two linear equations. Existing analysis provides only an upper bound for this regime.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of LowMC using linearization-based full-key recovery from compact differential trails.
assumptions: The attack is extended backward by more than b + r₃ rounds.
The regime satisfies b ≤ r₁ + r₂.
parameters: N: number of compact differential trails
b, r₁, r₂, and r₃: parameters defining the backward-round extension and its applicable regime
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find a simple, tight expected-time formula that accounts for both the additional linear equations and the extra variables needed to linearize inactive S-boxes.

citations.label: Cryptanalysis of Full LowMC and LowMC-M with Algebraic Techniques

progress.summary: The paper presents Equation 10 as only an upper bound in the extended-backward regime. It identifies the obstacle as the tradeoff between additional leaked equations and the variables needed to linearize inactive S-boxes.
